title: A constructible sheaf of modules on the spectrum of a field becomes constant over a finite separable extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring and $G$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $(\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], an object of $\Mod((\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then there are a finite separable field extension $K/k$, a finite $\Lambda$-module $M$ (finite as a set) and an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules $\pi^{-1}G\cong\underline M$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\Et}$, where $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the induced morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\pi^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $\underline M$ the constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with value $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

source.place: proof of Lemma 09Z6 (lemma-constructible-maps-into-constant), line 12969-12971: 'Since F is constructible, there is a finite separable extension K/kappa(x) such that F|_Spec(K) is the constant sheaf with value E for some finite set E' (stated without proof; the module form is that of part (3)); Definition 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant); literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex Lemma 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the stratification of a one-point space).* By [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] there is a stratification $(\iota_m:Z_m\to\operatorname{Spec}k)_{m<n}$ [def-constructible-stratification]: pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets $T_m$ covering $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and immersions $\iota_m$ with set-theoretic image $T_m$, such that every $\iota_m^{-1}G$ is finite locally constant in the sense of Stacks 03RU as spelled out in (b) of that definition. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has exactly one point (the zero ideal is the only prime of a field). As the $T_m$ cover this point and are pairwise disjoint, exactly one stratum, say $T_{m_0}$, is nonempty, and $T_{m_0}=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Put $Z=Z_{m_0}$, $\iota=\iota_{m_0}:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; then $Z\neq\emptyset$ (its image is $T_{m_0}\neq\emptyset$), $\iota$ is an immersion with image all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and by (b) there are an etale covering $\{u_i:U_i\to Z\}_{i\in I}$ (a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms) and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ with isomorphisms of sheaves of $\Lambda_{U_i}$-modules $\alpha_i:(\iota^{-1}G)|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{M_i}$. (Condition (a), constructibility of the strata, is not needed.)

source.place: Definition 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant), line 9917; the definition of constructible sheaves of Lambda-modules (Section 09Y5ff.) as recorded in def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\iota$ is an isomorphism).* The image of the immersion $\iota$ is all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, a closed subset, so $\iota$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion]. By the affine description of closed immersions in [def-weil-closed-immersion] (Stacks 01QO), applied to the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}k$ itself, there is an ideal $I\subseteq k$ with $\iota$ isomorphic over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(k/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. As $k$ is a field, $I=0$ or $I=k$; $I=k$ would give $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}(0)=\emptyset$, contradicting $Z\neq\emptyset$ (step 1). So $I=0$ and $\iota$ is isomorphic over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_k)=\mathrm{id}$, i.e. $\iota$ is an isomorphism of schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Lemma 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion): closed immersions into an affine scheme Spec(R) are Spec(R/I); agent-written argument, Stacks 09Z6 gives none

proof.text: *Step 3 (a point of some $U_i$ and its residue field; Stacks 02GL(2)).* Since $Z\neq\emptyset$ and the family $\{u_i\}$ is jointly surjective, there are $i\in I$ and a point $x\in U_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] there are an affine open $V\subseteq U_i$ containing $x$, a ring $B$ with $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ (via the open immersion $v:\operatorname{Spec}B\to U_i$ with image $V$), and a prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ corresponding to $x$. The composite $e=\iota\circ u_i\circ v:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]: $v$ is an open immersion, hence etale (1); $\iota$ is an isomorphism (step 2), in particular an open immersion, hence etale (1); $u_i$ is etale; and composites of etale morphisms are etale (2). By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] $e=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for a unique ring map $\varphi:k\to B$. The preimage $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ is a prime of $k$, hence $0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] (with $A=k$, $\mathfrak p=0$) the residue field $K:=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a finite separable extension of $\kappa(0)$ via the induced map. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] (1), $\kappa(0)$ is a fraction field of $k/0=k$ and $k\to\kappa(0)$ is injective with kernel $0$; since $k$ is a field, $k\to\kappa(0)$ is an isomorphism. Hence, with $\psi:k\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)=K$ (the composite equals $k\to\kappa(0)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, the residue field maps being induced by $\varphi$ on localizations), $K$ is a finite separable field extension of $k$ via $\psi$.

source.place: Lemma 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field) (2), line 8175: fibres of etale morphisms are disjoint unions of spectra of finite separable extensions; here only the residue field of one point is used

proof.text: *Step 4 (the morphism $\pi$ factors through $U_i$).* Let $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the canonical map $B\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)=K$, and $j=v\circ s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to U_i$. By functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\iota\circ u_i\circ j=e\circ s=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(B\to K)=\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=\pi$, the morphism induced by the extension $K/k$ of step 3.

source.place: proof of Lemma 09Z6 (lemma-constructible-maps-into-constant), line 12969-12971 ('F|_Spec(K)'): agent-written factorization

proof.text: *Step 5 (restriction to $U_i$ is the inverse image along $u_i$, $\Lambda$-linearly).* Put $H=\iota^{-1}G$, a sheaf of $\Lambda_Z$-modules [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) ($u_i$ is etale) there is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves $\rho_H:u_i^{-1}H\xrightarrow{\sim}H|_{U_i}$, and by its clause (2) its adjoint under $u_i^{-1}\dashv u_{i,*}$ is the map $H\to u_{i,*}(H|_{U_i})$ given at $W\in Z_{\Et}$ by the restriction map $H(W)\to H(W\times_ZU_i)$ of $H$ along the projection. Restriction maps of a sheaf of $\Lambda_Z$-modules are linear over the restriction maps of $\Lambda_Z$, which (through the identification $u_i^{-1}\Lambda_Z\cong\Lambda_{U_i}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (1) and the unit $\Lambda_Z\to u_{i,*}u_i^{-1}\Lambda_Z$) is how $\Lambda_Z$ acts on $u_{i,*}(H|_{U_i})$; so this adjoint is $\Lambda_Z$-linear, and by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction] $\rho_H$ is $\Lambda_{U_i}$-linear: an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules. Composing with $\alpha_i$ of step 1 gives $\beta_i=\alpha_i\circ\rho_H:u_i^{-1}\iota^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{M_i}$ on $(U_i)_{\Et}$.

source.place: Definition 03RU (restriction F|_{U_i}); agent-written identification with the inverse image

proof.text: *Step 6 (inverse images along the composite).* By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2), applied to $(u,v)=(\iota,u_i)$ and then to $(u,v)=(\iota\circ u_i,j)$, there are isomorphisms $c:j^{-1}u_i^{-1}\iota^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{-1}(\iota\circ u_i)^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}(\iota\circ u_i\circ j)^{-1}G=\pi^{-1}G$ (step 4), the first being $j^{-1}$ of $c_{\iota,u_i,G}$. Each $c_{u,v,G}$ is characterized in clause (2) as the map whose adjoint under the composite adjunction $v^{-1}u^{-1}\dashv u_*v_*$ is $d_{u,v}\circ\eta_{u\circ v,G}$; the unit $\eta_{u\circ v,G}$ is $\Lambda$-linear and $d_{u,v}$ is given on sections by the maps of the sheaf $(u\circ v)^{-1}G$ along isomorphisms of objects, hence $\Lambda$-linear, so by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction] (applied to $u$ and then to $v$) $c_{u,v,G}$ is $\Lambda$-linear; and $j^{-1}$ of a linear map is linear [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2). So $c$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $(\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\Et}$.

*Step 7 (the inverse image of a constant sheaf is constant; conclusion).* By [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] with values in $\Lambda$-modules there is an isomorphism $j^*\underline{M_i}_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, where $j^*$ is the left adjoint of the direct image on sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules; $j^{-1}$ on sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules is also left adjoint to that direct image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (3), so $j^{-1}\cong j^*$ by uniqueness of adjoints and $\gamma:j^{-1}\underline{M_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{M_i}$, the constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with value $M_i$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. With $M=M_i$, a finite $\Lambda$-module (step 1), the composite $\pi^{-1}G\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}j^{-1}u_i^{-1}\iota^{-1}G\xrightarrow{j^{-1}(\beta_i)}j^{-1}\underline{M_i}\xrightarrow{\gamma}\underline M$ (steps 5, 6) is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, and $K/k$ is finite separable (step 3). This is the statement.
